title: Geneva drive
description: A driver wheel with one pin steps a slotted wheel exactly a quarter turn each rotation, then locks it still; no motor, film or clock shown

facts.intro: Introduce a recognizable Geneva drive: an orange driver wheel with a red pin on the left and a steel four-slot wheel on the right. Everything is still.
facts.cutaway: A simplified cutaway lifts the small cover to expose the steel slotted wheel and the red pin of the driver wheel that is about to enter one slot.
facts.drive: Illustrated input force turns the driver wheel steadily. Its red pin slides into a slot of the steel wheel and pushes it, so the steel wheel turns exactly a quarter turn.
facts.response: Close-up of the pin leaving the slot. The pin slides out, the steel wheel stops after its quarter turn, and the rim of the driver wheel holds it still.
facts.hold: No part moves for this explanation. The driver wheel turns all the time, but the slotted wheel moves only while the pin is inside a slot. Between steps it sits locked.
facts.repeat: The driver wheel makes another full turn. The pin enters the next slot, steps the steel wheel another quarter turn, and leaves again.
facts.limit: The driver wheel turns the other way for one turn. The pin pushes the slotted wheel back a quarter turn, so the step happens in either direction.
facts.payoff: The cover closes. Driver and slotted wheel work together: a steady turn becomes stop-and-go steps of exactly a quarter turn. No motor or film is shown.
